LangGraph._comment: Offline dev default: the stub extractor is an explicit opt-in (D-E), never inferred from the environment. Set UseStubExtractor to false to drive the real isolated agent on a running `bun nx serve langgraph`. Host lives HERE and not in appsettings.json: a loopback host is correct only in Development, and as a base default it was what let a deployment silently call itself (issue #94). `langgraph dev` serves plain HTTP on :2024 — the production image listens on 8000.

Consent._comment: spec 14 §5.1 jurisdiction policy. JurisdictionPolicyProvider fail-closes to NoticeRequired=true when a channel is unconfigured, which is why every demo call opened by asking permission to record and waiting for an answer — the gate ENDs the turn until the customer replies, so it cost a full round trip before hello. Voice is set to notice-not-required HERE, in Development only: appsettings.json configures no Consent section, so every other environment keeps failing closed. The gate itself is untouched and still records a consent row (outcome 'not_required'), so the audit trail survives. Turning this off for a real deployment is a COMPLIANCE decision, not a UX one: most Australian states require consent to record a call, and the honest frictionless form is a notice that does not block ('This call may be recorded.') rather than no notice at all — set NoticeRequired true and give NoticeText to get that.

DatabaseBootstrap._comment: Development applies EF migrations at startup so a fresh `docker compose up` needs no manual `dotnet ef database update`. Stays false in appsettings.json for every other environment.

TenantContext._comment: spec-15 minted TenantContext TTL (seconds); short-lived — OD-3 placeholder.

TenantContextSigningKeys._comment: DEV-ONLY spec-15 JWS signing keys (base64 HMAC secrets). Never real secrets; production keys come from the secret store / vault.
